    What this guide covers

    Document Forensics

    Upload any document or photo and get back how risky it is, why, and exactly where on each page the problems are.

    Vehicle Insurance Claims

    Upload a vehicle claim's documents together and get back a risk level, a written assessment, cross-document checks and an indicative payable amount.

    Every request and response in this guide was run against the live service on 27 October 2026, using synthetic test documents. Long responses are shortened where marked with …

    1. Getting started

    Authentication

    Send your API key with every request, in either of these headers:

    Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here
X-API-Key: vk_your_key_here

    Base URL: https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app

    !

    Keep your key secret. Never put it in a web page or mobile app; call the API from your server. If a key leaks, delete it under API Keys in the Doxket app and create a new one.

    Check your key

    A quick way to confirm your key works and see which account it belongs to:

    GET/api/auth/me/
    REQUEST
    curl https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/auth/me/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here"
    RESPONSE · 200
    {
  "id": 42,
  "email": "mukherjee.inbox+test@voxket.ai",
  "role": "admin",
  "extended_access": true,
  "organization_slug": "mukherjee-inboxtests-organization",
  …
}

    extended_access must be true for the forensics and insurance APIs. If it is false, contact us.

    How both APIs work

    Both APIs are asynchronous. You upload, get an ID straight away, then check that ID until the work is done. Nothing is pushed to you, so keep checking at the intervals given in each section.

    2. Document Forensics API

    Upload a file, then fetch the result. The result tells you how risky the document is, why, and where on each page the problems are.

    2.1 Upload a file

    POST/api/forensics/scans/

    Send the file as multipart/form-data in a field named image.

    • Supported files: PDF, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP, WEBP
    • PDFs: up to 50 pages
    • One file per request. To check several files, upload each one separately.
    REQUEST
    curl -X POST https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/forensics/scans/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here" \
  -F "image=@hospital_bill.pdf"
    RESPONSE · 201
    {
  "scan_id": "6726de32-5909-4d80-8479-08198204fa02",
  "status": "queued",
  "precision_mode": true
}

    Save the scan_id; you need it to fetch the result. precision_mode tells you whether the deeper, layout-aware analysis is used for this scan. It is for information only.

    2.2 Get the result

    GET/api/forensics/scans/{scan_id}/

    A scan takes about one minute per page. All pages are checked together, so result stays null until the whole file is done.

    How often to check

    • Wait about 30 seconds after uploading, then check every 10 to 15 seconds.
    • Stop when status is completed, partial, requires_hitl or failed.
    • If a scan has not finished after 30 minutes, contact us with the scan_id.
    REQUEST
    curl https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/forensics/scans/6726de32-5909-4d80-8479-08198204fa02/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here"
    RESPONSE · 200, WHILE THE SCAN IS RUNNING
    {
  "id": "6726de32-5909-4d80-8479-08198204fa02",
  "status": "running",
  "created_at": "2026-10-27T08:17:24.189492Z",
  "media_type": "document",
  "page_count": 2,
  "result": null
}
    RESPONSE · 200, ONCE THE SCAN HAS FINISHED
    {
  "id": "6726de32-5909-4d80-8479-08198204fa02",
  "status": "completed",
  "created_at": "2026-10-27T08:17:24.189492Z",
  "media_type": "document",
  "page_count": 2,
  "result": {
    "label": "highly_risky",
    "risk_score": 0.98,
    "categories": ["tampered"],
    "summary": "This document has received a forensic score of 98 out of 100 and is classified as highly risky due to signs of tampering. It is not an original document, exhibiting copied stamp or signature marks across multiple pages. Furthermore, there are significant arithmetic and textual discrepancies regarding the total amounts.",
    "pages": [
      {
        "page": 1,
        "label": "highly_risky",
        "risk_score": 0.96
      },
      {
        "page": 2,
        "label": "highly_risky",
        "risk_score": 0.95
      }
    ],
    "findings": [
      {
        "severity": "risk",
        "title": "Copied stamp/sign (p.2)",
        "detail": "Pixel-identical on two scanned pages; a real stamp or signature never lands exactly the same twice.",
        "text": null,
        "page": 1,
        "box": [0.0718, 0.0501, 0.5277, 0.0302]
      },
      {
        "severity": "risk",
        "title": "Copied stamp/sign (p.1)",
        "detail": "Pixel-identical on two scanned pages; a real stamp or signature never lands exactly the same twice.",
        "text": null,
        "page": 2,
        "box": [0.0718, 0.0501, 0.5277, 0.0302]
      },
      {
        "severity": "concern",
        "title": "Totals don't add up",
        "detail": "Subtracting the advance payment of 5,000.00 from the gross amount of 24,574.00 equals 19,574.00, which does not match the printed net payable figure of 79,574.00. “Gross amount 24,574.00 Less: advance paid 5,000.00 Net payable 79,574.00”",
        "text": "Gross amount 24,574.00 Less: advance paid 5,000.00 Net payable 79,574.00",
        "page": 1,
        "box": [0.601, 0.461, 0.32, 0.075]
      },

        "text": "Net payable 79,574.00",
        "page": 1,
        "box": [0.603, 0.517, 0.318, 0.018]
      }
    ],
    "checks_passed": [
      "Pages agree",
      "Dates consistent",
      "Issuer consistent",
      "Not AI-generated"
    ]
  }
}

    What this result looks like on the page

    The test file was a two-page hospital bill. After it was printed, the net payable figure was changed from 19,574.00 to 79,574.00 in a slightly different typeface. The boxes below are drawn straight from result.findings: red for risk, orange for concern. The numbers follow the order of the findings on that page.

    #FindingWhat it means here
    1Copied stamp/sign (risk)The letterhead is pixel-identical on both pages. A scanned page never reproduces exactly; a digitally assembled one does.
    2Totals don't add up (concern)24,574.00 − 5,000.00 is 19,574.00, not the printed 79,574.00.
    3Amount in words differs (concern)The words still say “Nineteen Thousand Five Hundred Seventy-Four”.

    2.3 What the fields mean

    FieldMeaning
    idThe scan_id you got when uploading.
    statusWhere the scan is. See Status values below.
    media_typeWhat the file is: document, photo or object.
    page_countNumber of pages checked.
    resultThe outcome. null until the scan has finished.
    result.labelThe overall result. See Labels below.
    result.risk_scoreFrom 0 (no concerns) to 1 (very high risk).
    result.categoriesWhat kind of problem was found, if any. See Categories below. Empty when nothing was found.
    result.summaryA short written explanation of the result.
    result.pagesThe label and risk_score for each page. Use it to see which pages caused the result.
    result.findingsEach problem found. See Findings below.
    result.checks_passedChecks the file passed, e.g. “Dates consistent”. Shown for information; they do not lower the risk score.
    human_reviewOnly present after our team has reviewed the scan: decision, note and at (when).

    New fields may be added over time. Ignore any field you don’t recognise.

    Labels

    LabelMeaning
    highly_riskyStrong signs the document was edited, forged or generated. Don’t rely on it without checking.
    suspiciousSome warning signs. A person should check it.
    likely_authenticNo meaningful signs of tampering were found.

    Categories

    CategoryMeaning
    tamperedPart of a genuine document was changed, e.g. an amount, a date or a name.
    forgedThe document as a whole appears to be fabricated.
    ai_generatedThe page appears to be made or edited with an image generator.
    not_originalNot an original: e.g. a screenshot, a photo of a screen, or a copy reused from another document.

    Findings

    Each finding is one problem on one page:

    FieldMeaning
    severityrisk: strong evidence on its own. concern: a warning sign worth a look. warning: about where the file came from (e.g. not an original).
    titleA short name for the problem, e.g. “Totals don’t add up”.
    detailOne or two sentences explaining it. Can be null.
    textThe text the problem is about, as read from the page. null when it isn’t about specific text.
    pageThe page number, starting at 1.
    boxWhere it is on the page. See below. Can be null.

    Findings are sorted with the most serious first.

    Boxes

    A box is [x, y, width, height], each a fraction of the page from 0 to 1, measured from the top-left corner of the page as uploaded. To draw it on a page image W pixels wide and H pixels high:

    left   = x * W
top    = y * H
width  = width * W
height = height * H

    Page images

    GET/api/forensics/scans/{scan_id}/artifacts/page_image_{n}/

    Returns page n (from 1) as a PNG, exactly as it was checked, so you can draw the boxes on it. This URL works without the API key, so you can use it directly in an <img> tag. The scan_id is what protects it, so treat these URLs as confidential.

    REQUEST
    curl -o page_1.png \
  https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/forensics/scans/6726de32-5909-4d80-8479-08198204fa02/artifacts/page_image_1/

    2.4 Status values

    StatusMeaning
    queuedWaiting to start. Keep checking.
    runningIn progress. Keep checking.
    completedDone. The result is ready.
    partialDone, but some checks could not run. The result is still usable.
    requires_hitlDone, and flagged for review by our team. The result is ready now; the reviewer’s decision appears under human_review later.
    failedThe scan could not be completed. Upload the file again.

    3. Vehicle Insurance Claims API

    Review a vehicle claim as a whole. You open a case, upload the claim’s documents, start the analysis and fetch the result. Every document is read and checked for tampering. The documents are then compared with each other (same vehicle, same owner, valid licence, cover in force), the invoice arithmetic is checked, and an indicative payable amount is worked out under the policy.

    i

    The insurance API also needs Insurance switched on for your organisation. If your requests return “Insurance is not enabled for your organization”, contact us.

    3.1 Open a case

    POST/api/insurance/cases/

    Send JSON with your own claim reference. If a case with that reference already exists, a new one is still opened, with -dup01, -dup02 and so on added to the reference and duplicate_name set to true.

    REQUEST
    curl -X POST https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/cases/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reference": "CLM-2026-000184"}'
    RESPONSE · 201
    {
  "id": "b7687c02-1fd6-4acc-852c-f662e6048795",
  "claim_id": "367eea83-f535-4052-8870-ce7c91ec1415",
  "reference": "CLM-2026-000184",
  "status": "draft",
  "risk_level": null,
  "headline": "",
  "document_count": 0,
  "doc_types": [],
  "created_at": "2026-10-27T08:17:37.946250+00:00",
  "analysed_at": null,
  "duplicate_name": false
}

    Save the case id. The case starts as draft.

    3.2 Upload the claim’s documents

    POST/api/insurance/cases/{case_id}/files/

    Send multipart/form-data with one files field per file. Add a doc_types field holding a JSON list with one type per file, in the same order. Use "" for a file you want us to classify. You can call this more than once to add files before you start the analysis.

    doc_types valueDocument
    rcRegistration certificate
    dlDriving licence
    policyPolicy copy (current)
    previous_policyPrevious-year policy
    invoiceGarage / repair invoice
    vehicle_photoPhoto of the vehicle or the damage
    otherAnything else
    REQUEST
    curl -X POST https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/cases/b7687c02-1fd6-4acc-852c-f662e6048795/files/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here" \
  -F "files=@rc.jpg" \
  -F "files=@dl.jpg" \
  -F "files=@policy.pdf" \
  -F "files=@invoice.pdf" \
  -F 'doc_types=["rc","dl","policy","invoice"]'
    RESPONSE · 201 (SHORTENED)
    {
  "created": [
    {
      "claim_file_id": "8c512225-e7f9-4005-858c-85eb71fca61f",
      "document_id": "b99c3816-edef-4a3a-91ff-4cd73631e7f4",
      "filename": "rc.jpg",
      "reused_photo_matches_found": 0,
      "insurance_document_id": "e5457c6f-708c-4bfb-8b08-e2e562cdbc1f",
      "declared_type": "rc",
      "duplicate_within_claim": false
    },
    {
      "claim_file_id": "d6b9c8bf-a42e-4360-9c82-f69efb02cab1",
      "document_id": "639b6cd4-4be0-4e91-b0c3-6423f607b399",
      "filename": "dl.jpg",
      "reused_photo_matches_found": 0,
      "insurance_document_id": "ac431849-641a-4e09-9941-44311e8786af",
      "declared_type": "dl",
      "duplicate_within_claim": false
    },
    …
  ],
  "rejected": []
}

    Files that can’t be accepted are listed under rejected with the reason. duplicate_within_claim is true when the same photo was uploaded twice in this case. reused_photo_matches_found counts earlier claims in your organisation that used the same or a near-identical photo.

    3.3 Start the analysis

    POST/api/insurance/cases/{case_id}/run/

    Send an empty JSON object. You can run a case again after adding or correcting documents; each run replaces the previous result. Runs are charged in credits; if your balance doesn’t cover the run you get 402.

    REQUEST
    curl -X POST https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/cases/b7687c02-1fd6-4acc-852c-f662e6048795/run/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
    RESPONSE · 202
    {
  "status": "queued",
  "claim_pipeline": {
    "ocr_dispatched": 4,
    "forensics_dispatched": 0,
    "forensics_failed": 0
  }
}

    3.4 Get the result

    GET/api/insurance/cases/{case_id}/

    Wait about a minute after starting, then check every 15 to 30 seconds. Stop when status is done or failed. The four-document test claim below took just under two minutes.

    REQUEST
    curl https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/cases/b7687c02-1fd6-4acc-852c-f662e6048795/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here"
    RESPONSE · 200, ONCE DONE (SHORTENED)

    What this result looks like

    The test claim was a fictional Maruti Baleno claim with four documents. The garage invoice gives the registration as MH12 KD 4512, but the RC and policy say MH12 KD 4521. The licence expired months before the repair. The boxes come from analysis.evidence[].box_2d, and the card on the right is the case’s risk_level, coverage and narrative.findings.

    Besides the planted problems, the analysis also found that the invoice’s GST was over-added by ₹46 (₹10,250 printed against ₹10,204 correct), and that the garage’s GSTIN fails its check digit. It confirmed that the chassis number, engine number and owner name agree across the documents.

    3.5 What the fields mean

    The case

    FieldMeaning
    idThe case id.
    referenceYour claim reference.
    statusdraft (uploading), queued, running, done or failed.
    risk_levellow, medium or high. null until the first run is done.
    headlineOne sentence summing up the result.
    documentsOne entry per uploaded file. See below.
    analysisThe full result of the last run. See below.
    run_countHow many times the case has been analysed.
    analysed_atWhen the last run finished.
    error_messageWhy the run failed, when status is failed.

    Each document

    FieldMeaning
    idThe document id. Use it to correct the type (3.6) and to fetch page images (3.7).
    filenameThe file name you uploaded.
    doc_typeThe type used in the analysis: what you declared, otherwise what we detected.
    declared_type / detected_typeWhat you said the file is, and what we detected it as.
    pagesThe page numbers available as images.
    statuspending, done or failed for this document.
    forensics.scan_idThe tamper check for this document. Fetch it with GET /api/forensics/scans/{scan_id}/ for the full result, described in section 2.

    The analysis

    FieldMeaning
    analysis.statusdone when the analysis finished.
    analysis.verdict.bandlow, medium or high. The same as risk_level.
    analysis.verdict.admissibilityWhether the claim is payable under the policy at all, e.g. not_covered.
    analysis.narrative.headlineOne-sentence summary.
    analysis.narrative.summaryA short written assessment of the whole claim.
    analysis.narrative.findingsThe main points, each with title, detail and severity (high, medium or low). Matches between documents are listed too, as low.
    analysis.narrative.next_stepsSuggested follow-ups for your claims team.
    analysis.stages.coverageThe indicative settlement: payable (₹), own_damage_covered and own_damage_reason, compulsory_deductible, zero_depreciation, and lines (per invoice line: covered, payable, depreciation_percent, reason).
    analysis.evidenceWhere each fact was read. Items with kind crop have field, label (the text read), page, box_2d and image_url.

    box_2d is [top, left, bottom, right] on a 0–1000 scale of the page. That is not the same as the forensics box in section 2. To draw it on a page image W × H pixels: left = left/1000 × W, top = top/1000 × H, and so on. image_url is a path; add it to the base URL to get a PNG of that crop.

    !

    Build only on the fields listed above. Anything else inside analysis is internal working data. It may change or disappear without notice.

    3.6 Correct a document’s type

    PATCH/api/insurance/documents/{document_id}/

    If a file was classified wrongly, set its type and run the case again (3.3). Send "" to let us decide.

    REQUEST
    curl -X PATCH https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/documents/7a95b84c-43d9-4b6e-9349-f71fed61ec98/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"declared_type": "invoice"}'
    RESPONSE · 200
    {
  "pages": [
    {
      "number": 1
    }
  ],
  "id": "7a95b84c-43d9-4b6e-9349-f71fed61ec98",
  "claim_file_id": "ae9af002-87da-4471-8551-c8a495b0fdba",
  "document_id": "ec96ee6f-6eb6-4754-a4cf-9e0f869afe3b",
  "filename": "invoice.pdf",
  "file_extension": "pdf",
  "declared_type": "invoice",
  "detected_type": "",
  "doc_type": "invoice",
  "doc_type_label": "Garage invoice",
  "status": "done",
  "error_message": "",
  "ocr_status": "done",
  "forensics": {
    "scan_id": "8cd19f4a-ef21-4a5a-a2b2-e8de6389280d",
    "status": "completed",
    "label": "suspicious"
  }
}

    3.7 Page images

    GET/api/insurance/documents/{document_id}/pages/{n}/image/

    Returns page n of a document as a JPEG, at most 2000 pixels on its longer side. Like the forensics page images, it works without the API key so you can use it in an <img> tag; treat the URL as confidential.

    REQUEST
    curl -o invoice_p1.jpg \
  https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/documents/7a95b84c-43d9-4b6e-9349-f71fed61ec98/pages/1/image/

    3.8 List and delete cases

    GET/api/insurance/cases/?search={text}&page={n}

    Your organisation’s cases, newest first, 25 per page. search matches part of the reference.

    REQUEST
    curl "https://backend-production-8acf.up.railway.app/api/insurance/cases/?search=CLM-2026" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer vk_your_key_here"
    RESPONSE · 200
    {
  "count": 1,
  "page": 1,
  "page_size": 25,
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "b7687c02-1fd6-4acc-852c-f662e6048795",
      "claim_id": "367eea83-f535-4052-8870-ce7c91ec1415",

    DELETE/api/insurance/cases/{case_id}/

    Deletes the case and all its documents. Returns 204 with no body. This can’t be undone.

    4. Case studies

    Two real runs through this API, made on 27 October 2026 with the same calls shown in sections 2 and 3. Unlike the rest of this guide, these use real documents. Names, addresses, ID numbers, faces and the names of the hospital, insurer and garage are blurred, and vehicle numbers are blurred inside red boxes.

    4.1 Document Forensics: a hospital in-patient bill

    The file was one scanned page of a hospital's in-patient final bill, sent to POST /api/forensics/scans/ exactly as in 2.1. Nothing else was sent with it.

    What came back

    result.labelhighly_risky
    result.risk_score0.95 (shown as 95/100)
    result.categoriestampered
    result.summary“This document has received a forensic score of 95 out of 100 and is classified as highly risky due to clear signs of tampering. The file appears to be a manipulated copy rather than an original record, showing strong evidence of inserted entries and placeholder template text. Multiple alignment and visual rendering anomalies further indicate that content was added after the initial document was created.”
    #FindingWhat it means here
    1Leftover template text (risk)The ward is “DUMMY WARD BILLING / 4”: placeholder text from a billing template, not a real ward. Genuine bills are printed from live records.
    2Inserted value (risk)The ₹7,500.00 room-rent amount. Two independent checks agree: its ink tone differs from its row and column, and it is printed differently from the amounts around it.
    3Level on a tilted page (concern)This receipt line sits perfectly level while the scanned lines around it tilt by about 1.07°, which is what text added after scanning looks like.
    4Words off their line (concern)“68,830.00” sits 5.8 px higher than the words beside it.
    5Words off their line (concern)“Rs.” sits 3.7 px lower than the words beside it, on the same line.
    6Typed differently (concern)“Individual” has a different print or scan texture from the other filled-in values.

    Checks that passed (result.checks_passed): Totals add up, Dates consistent, Issuer consistent, PAN valid, Not AI-generated. So the arithmetic and dates are consistent; the risk comes from how the values were put on the page.

    4.2 Vehicle Insurance Claims: one claim, five documents

    A case was opened (3.1), five files were uploaded in one call with their types (3.2): the registration certificate, driving licence, policy, garage invoice and one photo of the car, and the analysis was started (3.3). It finished in about one minute.

    What came back

    The findings below are listed in analysis.narrative.findings.

    risk_levelhigh
    analysis.verdict.admissibilitynot_covered
    payable₹0 of ₹31,856.74 billed
    headline“Claim is inadmissible due to mismatched vehicle identities across all records and repairs occurring after policy expiration.”
    #FindingWhat it means here
    1Different vehicle across documents (high)The RC, policy schedule, and invoice all specify different registration numbers, chassis numbers, engine numbers, and models (Volkswagen Polo, Hyundai Verna, and XEV 9E).
    2Photo plate does not match (high)The vehicle photograph shows license plate MH46 •• 7599, which does not match the RC, the policy schedule, or the invoice.
    3Policy expired before repair (high)The policy coverage ended on 27 September 2026, but the repair order was dated 13 October 2026 and invoiced on 19 October 2026, leaving all billed lines uncovered.
    4Billed part not visibly damaged (medium)The acoustic windshield replacement billed at ₹19,620 shows no visible cracks or chips in the submitted photograph.
    5Vehicle owner and insured differ (medium)The registration certificate and the policy are in two different people’s names.
    6Registration expired before repair (low)The vehicle registration certificate expired on 12 October 2026, one day prior to the repair order date.

    One claim, four different vehicles

    #DocumentRegistration number and vehicle
    1Registration certificateUP32 •• 2870, Volkswagen Polo 1.2
    2PolicyMH47 •• 5963, Hyundai Verna 1.5
    3Garage invoiceMP09 •• 6756, Mahindra XEV 9e
    4Photo of the car (number plate read from the image)MH46 •• 7599

    Each document also gets its own tamper check, reported under documents[].forensics; fetch the full result with GET /api/forensics/scans/{scan_id}/ as in 2.2. The claim-level findings above come from comparing the documents with each other, which no single-document check can do.

    Suggested next steps (analysis.narrative.next_steps):

    • Repudiate the claim due to policy expiration prior to loss and vehicle identity mismatch
    • Request clarification from the claimant regarding conflicting registration, policy, and invoice documents
    • Refer the file to the investigation team for review of misrepresentation and conflicting vehicle records

    5. Errors

    Errors return JSON with a detail message, for example:

    {"detail": "Upload the claim's documents first."}
    CodeMeaning
    400The request is incomplete or invalid: an unsupported or oversized file, a PDF over 50 pages, no claim reference, no files, an unknown document type, or starting a case that has no documents.
    402Not enough credits for this insurance run. Top up, then retry.
    403Missing or invalid API key (“Authentication credentials were not provided.” / “Invalid or revoked API key.”), or your key doesn’t have access to this API. Contact us for access.
    404Not found, or it belongs to another organisation.
    409The case’s analysis is already running. Wait for it to finish.
    429Too many requests. Wait a few seconds and retry.
    503The service is temporarily unavailable. Retry shortly.
